source_text: Primo, supercilio stuporem suum aedificant Marcionitae, quod nouum deum proferant, quasi nos ueteris dei pudeat. inflantur et pueri nouis calceis, sed a uetere paedagogo calceati mox uanam gloriam uapulabunt. nouum igitur audiens deum, in uetere mundo et in uetere aeuo et sub uetere deo ignotum inauditum, quem, tantis retro saeculis neminem et ipsa ignorantia antiquum, quidam Iesus Christus, et ille in ueteribus nominibus nouus, reuelauerit, nec alius antehac. gratias ago huic gloriae eorum, maximo adiutorio eius hinc iam haeresim probaturus, nouae scilicet diuinitatis professionem. haec erit nouitas, quae etiam ethnicis deos peperit nouo, semper ac nouo titulo consecrationis cuiusque. quis deus nouus nisi falsus? ne Saturnum quidem tanta hodie antiquitas deum probabit, quia et illum nouitas aliquando produxerit.. cum primum consecrauit. atenim uiua et germana diuinitas nec de nouitate nec de uetustate, sed de sua ueritate cense-!i tur. non habet tempus aeternitas. omne enim tempus ipsa, est. quod facit, pati non potest. caret aetate quod non licet\' nasci. deus si est uetus, non erit, si est nouus, non fuit., nouitas initium testificatur, uetustas finem comminatur. deus autem tam alienus ab initio et fine est quam a tempore, arbitro et metatore initii et finis.I
pass_a_gloss: First, the Marcionites build their amazement on the basis of their forehead, because they bring forth a new God, as if we should be ashamed of the old God. Even children are puffed up with new shoes, but soon, having been shod by the old teacher, they will suffer the penalty of vain glory. Therefore, when I hear of a new God, unknown and unheard of in the old world and in the old age and under the old God, whom Jesus Christ, and He in the old names new, has revealed, and no other before this, I give thanks for this glory of theirs, which will be a great help to me in proving their heresy from now on, namely the profession of a new divinity. This will be the novelty that has also produced new gods for the Gentiles with a new and always new title of consecration for each one. What new God is there except a false one? Not even Saturn, with such great antiquity today, will be proven to be God, because novelty has also produced Him at some point, when He was first consecrated. For living and genuine divinity is not judged by novelty or antiquity, but by its own truth. Eternity does not have time. For all time is itself. What it does, it cannot suffer. What is not allowed to be born is without age. If God is old, He will not be; if He is new, He was not. Novelty testifies to a beginning, antiquity threatens an end. But God is as alien to beginning and end as to time, being the judge and measure of beginning and end.

choices.why: refers to a God that is new or recently introduced
refers to a God that is old or established
refers to the quality of being new or original

pass_b_english: First, the Marcionites build their amazement on their foreheads, because they bring forth a new God, as if we should be ashamed of the old God. Even children are puffed up with new shoes, but soon, shod by the old teacher, they will be flogged for their vain glory. Therefore, when I hear of a new God, unknown and unheard of in the old world, in the old age, and under the old God, whom Jesus Christ—and He, new in the old names—has revealed, and no one before this, I give thanks for this glory of theirs, which will be a great help to me from now on in proving their heresy, namely the profession of a new divinity. This will be the novelty that has also produced new gods for the Gentiles, with a new and ever-new title of consecration for each. What new God is there except a false one? Not even Saturn will be proven God by such great antiquity today, because novelty also produced him at some point, when he was first consecrated. For living and genuine divinity is judged not by novelty or antiquity, but by its own truth. Eternity does not have time; for all time is itself. What it does, it cannot suffer. What is not allowed to be born lacks age. If God is old, He will not be; if He is new, He was not. Novelty testifies to a beginning; antiquity threatens an end. But God is as alien to beginning and end as to time, being the judge and measure of beginning and end.
